scope: Three items, red first: (1) the re-pin to wolf 0.2.38 and lupin 0.1.60 with every wolf fixture built -g; (2) sniff#10, the startup margin of startup-wolf-large-dwarf; (3) S5 on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64: hardware watchpoints (watch, rwatch, awatch) and expressions (field access, indexing, arithmetic). Two PRs: the re-pin and #10 first, S5 second. The PAX half of S5 is drafted for a px lane, not built.

measured_before_code.what: where sniff's startup goes on the large-DWARF fixture, before any change
measured_before_code.how: sniff built by wolf 0.2.37 at the base 5ceae8e; fixtures/wolf/scalars built by 0.2.37 (default), 0.2.38 (default) and 0.2.38 -g; the script is `break helper` alone (load and resolve, no process started). CPU from the child rusage, minimum of 9; attribution by valgrind 3.27.1 callgrind instruction counts (Ir), which a shared host cannot perturb. A Linux host, native, single-threaded light slot; no process was traced.

fixture.note: the wolf units are a few hundred bytes; the size is the linked runtime's Rust DWARF (DWARF 4), as R-sn02-5 said. 0.2.38 grows .debug_info by 0.07% and .debug_frame is 184 bytes: the re-pin does not move this row.

breakdown_inclusive.phase: load_dwarf's subprogram scan, program.lu:385 (`!p.info.entries[e].is_null && p.info.entries[e].tag == 46`, about 1190 Ir per entry over 553175 entries)
everything else (ELF, sections, qualified names, file interning)

measured_before_code.conclusion: the cost is in sniff: 99.4% of startup is load_dwarf, and three eager passes that need no laziness (the subprogram scan, the reference validation and the line sort) are 42% of it.

R-sn05-1.question: #10: cut sniff's startup on large DWARF (A), or set the margin from measured runner spread (B)?

options.A: cut it in sniff, with no change to what is read or printed: (1) the subprogram scan over a local view of the entries (or the DIE pass records subprogram indexes), (2) reference validation by a bitset of entry starts instead of a binary search per reference, (3) the line sort by ascending runs (3056 runs in 129077 rows; the order (addr, ord) is total, so any correct sort gives the same list), (4) fast paths in dwarf_form and uint_le for the fixed-width forms. Then re-derive the margin from the measured spread.
options.A-lazy: per-unit lazy DIE loading. Every session use of an entry index (values, types, frames, locals) changes, and S5 adds type walking on top. Held back unless (A) misses its target.
options.B: keep the code; raise the margin to about 7.0 (the hosted maximum 6.06 times 1.15). It leaves a 6x-slower-than-gdb startup in place and stops the row from catching a regression of less than 15%.
options.C: run the row on the local record only (issue option 2). It hides the hosted signal the row exists to give.
options.D: compare with sniff's own earlier time (issue option 3). Hosted runners differ in CPU model; sniff's own minimum moved 0.72-0.99 s across five hosted runs, a wider spread than the ratio's 4.80-6.06.

R-sn05-1.recommend: A, then the margin re-derived. The cost is in sniff, and (1)-(3) are 42% of it with no semantic change.
R-sn05-1.margin_derivation: hosted over local, from five hosted runs (4.80, 5.36, 5.83, 6.06, 6.02) against the local record 4.25 of the same code: a factor of 1.13 to 1.43. The new margin is the local ratio after the cut times 1.43 (the worst hosted runner seen) times 1.25 (headroom for a runner type not yet seen), rounded up to the next 0.5. It is written in the note with the numbers it came from, and checked against the PR's hosted run.

R-sn05-2.question: S5's scope in this lane

options.a: the contract's two items only (watchpoints; print with field access, indexing and arithmetic)
options.b: (a) plus the index's thin additions over the same evaluator: conditional breakpoints (`break X if E`, `condition N E`) and `display`, and printing wolf's aggregates as 0.2.38's DWARF describes them

R-sn05-2.recommend: b, built in that order, with (a) the part that must land for the second PR; whatever of (b) does not fit is listed in the note as S5's remainder.

R-sn05-3.question: the expression grammar for C frames and for wolf frames

options.a: one grammar for both: sniff's own C-subset parser grown with `.`, `->`, `[]` and comparisons
options.b: fenrir's front end (vendored at a pin) for frames whose unit's producer is wolf, and sniff's C-subset parser for C frames. 0.2.38 keeps DW_LANG_C11 on wolf units, so the language is taken from DW_AT_producer, not DW_AT_language

R-sn05-3.recommend: b: the track ruled that wolf expressions go through fenrir's front end and that what it does not cover is refused by name; C rows are held to gdb's C.

watchpoints_linux.mechanism: DR0-DR3 hold addresses, DR7 enables them, DR6 says which fired (Intel SDM vol. 3, ch. 18). Written through PTRACE_POKEUSER and read through PTRACE_PEEKUSER at offsetof(struct user, u_debugreg[i]), measured by tools/abi-probe.c (a new `user u_debugreg N` line), never read from header text (R-sn02-3).
watchpoints_linux.dr7: L0-L3 enable bits 0, 2, 4, 6; R/W at bits 16+4n (01 write, 11 read or write); LEN at bits 18+4n (00 one byte, 01 two, 11 four, 10 eight); the address aligned to its length. x86 has no read-only data breakpoint, so rwatch is R/W 11.
watchpoints_linux.stop: a data breakpoint traps after the access with SIGTRAP; DR6 B0-B3 name the slot, and sniff clears DR6 before resuming.
watchpoints_linux.commands: watch, rwatch, awatch on a variable (a local or a global, a field or an element); info watchpoints; delete; info breakpoints lists them; a watch on a local is deleted when its frame returns, with gdb's message.
watchpoints_linux.output_predicted: gdb's words: `Hardware watchpoint N: x`, then at a hit a blank line, `Old value = ...`, `New value = ...` and the frame line; `Hardware read watchpoint N: x` and `Value = ...`; `Hardware access (read/write) watchpoint N: x` with `Value = ...` or Old/New. What gdb does when an rwatch'd variable is written (x86 cannot tell a read from a write) is taken from its transcript, not predicted.
watchpoints_linux.refused_by_name: a fifth hardware slot, an expression wider than the slots can cover, and every software watchpoint (`set can-use-hw-watchpoints 0`): sniff has no single-stepping watcher.
watchpoints_linux.rows: a new C fixture (c/watch: a global, a local in a loop, a struct field, an array element, a write of the same value) by gcc and clang -O0, each row held to the pinned gdb; a wolf fixture (wolf/watch) held to gdb's text and to lupin's values at each stop

watchpoints_macos.mechanism: ARM_DEBUG_STATE64's __wvr/__wcr through thread_set_state (the state block single step already uses). WCR from the Arm ARM: E, PAC (EL0), LSC (01 load, 10 store, 11 both), BAS (the bytes of an 8-byte aligned doubleword).
watchpoints_macos.stop: EXC_BREAKPOINT with the data-abort code and the address in the subcode, before the access completes. sniff disables the slot, single-steps, re-enables and reports after the access, so Old/New values match the Linux rows.
watchpoints_macos.slots: the count is probed from the state the kernel keeps, never assumed
watchpoints_macos.rows: the Linux watch rows run on the Mac (the S3 mechanism, named drops only), plus lldb-fact rows (watchpoint set variable, the stop reason, old and new values)

expressions.front_end: fenrir's front end vendored at a recorded pin under src/vendor/, its licence and pin beside it; a wolf frame's `print` text is parsed by it as an expression. Node kinds it parses that sniff does not evaluate are refused by name.
expressions.evaluated: names (locals, args, globals), integer, float and bool literals, `.field`, `[index]`, unary - and !, binary + - * / % and the comparisons, parentheses, $N history; in C frames also `*`, `&` and `->`.
expressions.c_rows: held to the pinned gdb byte for byte: `p a.b[2]`, `p x + 1`, `p a.b[1] * 3 - x`, `p ptr->b[0]`, `p *ptr`, `p a.nosuch` (`There is no member named nosuch.`), `p x[0]` on a scalar (`cannot subscript something of type `int'`), `p 1/0` (`Division by zero`)
expressions.wolf_rows: a struct with scalar fields and a List[int] field: gdb prints what the DWARF describes (fields by name); `p a.count + 1` and field access held to gdb; `p a.items[2]` (an index through a List's header) is something gdb cannot do on a header struct, so its value is held to lupin's at the same stop
expressions.conditional_and_display: if R-sn05-2 (b): `break X if E` and `condition N E` evaluate E at each hit and stop when it is nonzero; `display E` prints `N: E = V` at each stop. Held to gdb on C.
